text:
anika: quick heads-up — I'm starting a migration proposal: unify per-route quota metadata + route labels into a single `route_profile_v2` table to avoid joining across 3 tables in console queries. want to surface tradeoffs before i write the PR.
matt: +1 to fewer joins. curious: is this denorm or materialized view? performance vs write complexity tradeoff.
anika: leaning denorm for read perf. writes would atomically upsert route_profile_v2 from existing joins during commit path. can do dual-write for 2 weeks while backfilling.
lei: we need to consider cardinality explosion — some customers create thousands of routes with many labels. denorm could bloat storage and slow writes. what's the expected size? any numbers?
anika: rough estimate: 15k active routes across prod clusters, avg 6 labels per route -> route_profile_v2 ~ 90k rows, each row ~1.2KB -> ~108MB per cluster. acceptable but worry about frequent label updates.
jordan: also watch telemetry side — current console p99 queries stitch route -> quota -> usage counters. If we replace joins with a denorm, we change which telemetry fields are authoritative. need an invariant plan.
anika: proposal: canonical write path remains route metadata service; it writes canonical row and we emit an event to telemetry pipeline to update aggregated counters. route_profile_v2 is a eventually-consistent projection owned by console service.
olga: how will rollouts work? console UX relies on up-to-date quotas during admin changes. eventual consistency could show stale quota in UI for seconds -> bad UX.
matt: can we keep a fast cache for recent edits (Redis) and read-through to provide strong consistency for recent writes? stale is ok for analytics but not for admin screens.
anika: yes, plan B: read-through cache on write path for admin endpoints; analytics queries hit route_profile_v2 only. simplifies queries for dashboards and graphs.
deploy-bot: deploy checklist generated: 1) dualwrite adapter in route-meta service 2) projection pipeline job 3) backfill/validator 4) canary read route_profile_v2 for query endpoints 5) cache warmup and eviction policy.
lei: backfill validator is important. we should compare samples: compute diff for shard range to ensure parity before cutover. also gate by false-positive tolerance (<=0.1%).
jordan: rolling cutover should include fallback to old joins for a percent of queries for 24h. circuit breaker on error rate/latency.
anika: agree. UX for rollouts: add admin feature flag to enable unified profile per org; start with internal orgs then beta customers.
matt: one more: what about historical telemetry? dashboards that aggregate over time use the old envelope schema. migrating to denorm may require re-ingesting or a query adapter that reads older records and projects into new shape.
anika: plan is adapter layer for historical queries that rewrites predicates and uses existing event store to reconstruct profile for time buckets. that'll be slower but only used for longrange queries.
olga: security/compliance check: ensure route_profile_v2 doesn't leak PII and honors tenant isolation labels. add KMS tag to rows? probably not necessary but flag for review.
anika: noted. action items: (a) i'll draft the migration PR + schema DDL (b) matt + lei to prototype write-path dualwrite + cache behavior (c) jordan to spec telemetry validator and backfill diff script (d) olga to sign off on rollout gating and security checklist. expected PR by EOD Thurs.
matt: happy to pair on the dualwrite prototype Thurs morning.
lei: i'll sketch the backfill diff job today and post results.
jordan: will mock the canary query fallback and failure modes.
olga: will review the compliance surface Monday.
anika: thanks everyone :thumbsup: I'll post the design doc in #eng-platform once PR is open. keep discussion here for blockers.
